children: Shares of Travelers declined in premarket trading on Friday even as the property and casualty insurer's quarterly earnings came in well above Wall Street expectations.

Travelers stock fell 5.2% to $367 in premarket trading on Friday after ending Thursday up 1.6%. The Dow Jones Industrial Average component has risen 32% this year as of the closing bell on Thursday. It hit a record closing high of $397.22 on July 28.
Travelers on Friday posted core earnings of $9.18 a share in the third quarter, up from $8.14 a year ago and handily beating Wall Street's expectation for $7.39.
The company said its quarterly earnings performance was due to higher net investment income, which was partially offset by higher catastrophe losses.
Net premiums written totaled $11.48 billion, essentially flat from last year and coming in above the analyst consensus forecast of $11.36 billion, according to FactSet.
Catastrophe losses, net of reinsurance, in the quarter increased 34% to $538 million from $402 million a year ago.
